note: Full LLM judge requires OPENAI_API_KEY in .env. This file shows the expected output format and a sample of human ratings for comparison. Run `python src/llm_judge.py` after configuring the API key to generate real scores.

how_agreement_is_measured.computation: For each of the 5 rating dimensions, we compare the human rating (1-5) with the LLM judge score (1-5) across 35 rows. Pearson r measures linear agreement. r=1.0 means perfect agreement, r=0 means no correlation.
how_agreement_is_measured.expected_range: Literature reports LLM-human agreement of r=0.7–0.9 for GPT-4 class models on structured rubrics (Zheng et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2023).
how_agreement_is_measured.code: See src/llm_judge.py → pearson() function and run_judge() method

why_deferred.reason: LLM judge requires a paid API key (OPENAI_API_KEY). The infrastructure (rubric, Pearson computation, human ratings) is fully built and tested. To activate: set OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... in .env and run `python src/llm_judge.py`.

citations: Zheng et al. (2023). Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena. NeurIPS 2023.
Liu et al. (2023). G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment. EMNLP 2023.
